title: Athena: querying S3 in place, partitions and the bytes scanned

videos.script: Athena answers SQL about files that never leave S3. There is nothing to load and nothing to keep running. {{bucket}} That sounds free, and it is not. Athena charges for every byte it reads, and the same question can read forty megabytes or a hundred and sixty kilobytes. {{bytes}} This lesson puts a month of Quitanda's orders into the lake. That is three quarters of a million orders, once as CSV and once as Parquet. {{lake}} moto accepts an Athena query and runs none of it. So you will ask your questions with DuckDB, inside a small program. That program counts each byte it pulls out of S3. {{count}} Then the same question four ways. All of the CSV, then two columns of the Parquet, then one day of each. {{four}} You will see where every byte went, down to the footer at the end of each file. {{footer}} Last come the limits that stop a careless query from reading the whole lake. A workgroup, partition projection, and a query that writes a table. {{guard}}
